Olga —

Thanks for sharing the draft MSA. We've pulled together a round of redlines focused on the limitation of liability and damages carve-outs. High level: we cannot accept an unlimited or near-unbounded exposure tied to a multiple-of-fees construct without a per-year anchor. Our suggested positions are listed below and tracked in the attached redlines (ACME_MSA_Redlines.docx):

- Replace any aggregate-terminology with a "12-month rolling" or "annualized" cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months.
- Prefer a fixed multiplier (1x annual fees) rather than a cumulative multiple of fees over the entire term.
- Keep consequential damages excluded, but we ask to explicitly carve back consequential damages for data breach and IP infringement so those remain recoverable.
- Exclude claims arising from gross negligence and willful misconduct from the cap.

We know you have a different view on commercial risk allocation. Can you send one clean proposed paragraph (redline) that reconciles these points so we can run it by procurement/legal?

Ben —

Appreciate the clear ask and the tracked redlines. I attached a short proposal (liability-language-proposal.docx) that attempts to bridge our positions and keep the deal moving. Summary of our compromise approach:

- Primary cap: rolling 12-month cap equal to the fees paid in the preceding 12 months ("Annualized Fees"). This addresses your ask for a per-year anchor.
- Aggregate/term cap: where the contract term exceeds 12 months, the total liability cap will be the greater of (i) 3x Annualized Fees or (ii) fees actually paid during the Term (to protect you on short-term usage patterns).
- Carve-outs: losses resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct will not be capped. We are prepared to accept carve-ins that permit recovery for data breach and IP infringement, but only to the extent caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Consequential damages: remain excluded, with the limited exception for statutory indirect damages that cannot be excluded under applicable law.

Why this structure: it gives ACME a predictable 12-month exposure while bounding Redwood's cumulative exposure over a long-term engagement. From a commercial perspective it ties risk to actual consumption (Annualized Fees) and keeps a finite multiplier to satisfy finance/legal covenants.

If that sounds directionally reasonable, I'll ask Legal/Finance for a short internal review and then send you a clean clause to insert back into the doc.

Ben / ACME team —

Thanks for the redlines and patience while we aligned internally. Below is the clause Redwood proposes to replace the current liability section. If this is acceptable, we'll incorporate into the tracked MSA and route for signature (DocuSign link below). If you want any narrow tweaks (e.g., different multiplier or floor), call out the single line and we can iterate quickly.

PROPOSED LIABILITY LANGUAGE (for insertion into Section X):

"For purposes of this Agreement, 'Annualized Fees' means the total Fees actually paid by Customer to Redwood during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the relevant claim arose. The aggregate liability of Redwood for all Claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) three times (3x) the Annualized Fees or (b) the Fees actually paid by Customer under this Agreement during the Term. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Party shall be liable to the other for consequential, incidental, punitive or special damages, except to the extent such damages result from (i) a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (ii) statutory liability that cannot be excluded under applicable law. "

Additional terms: (i) "Fees" means invoiced amounts collected by Redwood (no retroactive adjustments to reduce Fees after a claim), (ii) a minimum liability floor of $25,000 will apply to agreements where Annualized Fees would otherwise be zero, and (iii) the parties agree that third-party obligations and liabilities arising from components not controlled by Redwood (including cloud provider outages) will be excluded from Redwood's cap.

Next steps: if you agree in principle, I'll update the tracked MSA and send a DocuSign packet. Otherwise, please indicate which single element you want to change (multiplier, floor, carveout language) and we'll respond within 24 hours.
